plan.topic: Is your semaglutide or tirzepatide the real thing? Compounded and counterfeit GLP-1s: what's confirmed
plan.angle: 'Compounded and counterfeit GLP-1s aren't the same thing. Here's what's confirmed.' (1) Branded semaglutide/tirzepatide are FDA-approved. Compounded versions are not FDA-approved or reviewed. (2) Bloomberg reported on Oct 15, 2026 that FDA inspectors found mould and falsified records at 2 overseas plants making ingredients for compounded versions, now on import alert. (3) UK: on Oct 14, 2026, MHRA and police seized over 12,000 fake tirzepatide and retatrutide pens (GOV.UK). (4) In one US online survey (Obesity Science & Practice, primary URL), photos showed 25.8% were on compounded products, and most of them believed they were on a brand. Close: ask your prescriber or pharmacist which product you're on; don't stop or change your medicine on your own. Prescriber line.

plan.why: Calm warnings about gray-market products are a lane that works for us (165 and 58). Tirzepatide is in the title, and the rising news this week is a fresh story, separate from the 10-16 retatrutide piece. | fact-check: Sources exist. (a) Bloomberg, Oct 15, 2026: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-15/compound-semaglutide-tirzepatide-plants-in-china-found-with-black-mold-by-fda reports FDA inspectors found mould, contamination and falsified records at 2 Chinese plants making semaglutide/tirzepatide ingredients for compounding, and FDA placed both on import alert. Attribute it as 'Bloomberg reported that FDA inspectors found…'. Do not name the plants. (b) MHRA on GOV.UK: 'Counterfeit weight loss pens worth £2 million seized by MHRA and West Midlands Police' https://www.gov.uk/government/news/counterfeit-weight-loss-pens-worth-2-million-seized-by-mhra-and-west-mids-police (Oct 14, 2026; >12,000 fake retatrutide and tirzepatide pens, Birmingham). Specify UK, the date, and that retatrutide isn't approved anywhere. (c) The Obesity Science & Practice photo study exists (322 US adults from an online research panel, Oct 2025–Jan 2026; 83 = 25.8% on compounded products by photo; about two-thirds of those reported a brand-name drug). It is confirmed only via Medscape (paywalled). The scriptwriter MUST cite the Wiley/PubMed primary URL. If no primary URL can be found, drop the stat. Say 'in one US online survey', since the sample isn't representative. Keep COMPOUNDED (legal in some circumstances, not FDA-approved) clearly separate from COUNTERFEIT (fake, illegal). Never imply that compounded = counterfeit, or that pharmacy-dispensed branded pens are likely fake. Calm tone, no emoji, no sellers or prices, no tips on spotting fakes that read as buying guidance.

package.title: Compounded vs Counterfeit Semaglutide/Tirzepatide: Confirmed? #shorts
package.description:
Compounded isn't counterfeit. Compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide aren't FDA-approved, though they can be appropriate in limited situations. Bloomberg (Oct 15, 2026) reported mold at one Chinese plant and quality problems at another — both make ingredients for compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide, now on FDA import alert (Sept–Oct 2026). Counterfeit = fake: on Oct 14, 2026 the UK's MHRA and police seized 12,000+ fake tirzepatide and retatrutide pens (retatrutide isn't approved anywhere as of Oct 2026).

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Don't stop or change your medicine on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary: I checked every claim. FDA's page (current as of Oct 1, 2026) confirms that compounded drugs aren't FDA-approved and aren't reviewed for safety, effectiveness or quality, and that compounding can be appropriate in limited situations. The GOV.UK/MHRA release (published Oct 15, 2026) confirms the Oct 14 seizure by the MHRA and West Midlands Police of more than 12,000 fake tirzepatide and retatrutide pens, and that retatrutide isn't authorised in the UK. Bloomberg's page returns a 403, but the Oct 15, 2026 report exists, and NewsNation, Quartz and Bloomberg's own X post confirm the details: two Chinese plants making semaglutide and tirzepatide ingredients for compounded GLP-1s (Chengdu Shengnuo: black mold and hidden lab papers; Nanjing Chengong: relabelling other makers' ingredients without checking their test data), both reported as on FDA Import Alert 66-40 (Sep 19 and Oct 1, 2026). FDA's own import-alert page loaded only partly, so I couldn't confirm either firm on it directly. The framing separates compounded from counterfeit, names no sellers, carries the prescriber line and the don't-stop-or-change line, and runs about 167 words. Only minor fixes are needed.

issues.claim: FDA put both on import alert.
issues.problem: Accurate, but the status isn't dated. The craft notes ask for every status to be dated, and the import alerts came before the Oct 15 report (Sep 19 and Oct 1, 2026, per the coverage of Bloomberg's report).
issues.fix: Replace the last sentence with: "Both make ingredients for compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide, and FDA put both on import alert in September and October." (Optional: this adds 4 words and takes the narration to about 171, over the 170-word cap. If you use it, trim elsewhere, e.g. change "Now the news." in s3 to "News:".)

issues.claim: Compounded versions can be legal in some situations
issues.problem: True (compounding is legal under US law), but FDA's page puts it as clinical appropriateness: only when an FDA-approved drug can't meet the patient's need or isn't available. Matching FDA's scope is more precise.
issues.fix: "Compounded versions can be appropriate in limited situations, like a shortage or a medical need an approved drug can't meet, but they're not FDA-approved, and FDA doesn't review them for safety, effectiveness or quality." (Optional: this is about 9 words longer, taking the narration to about 176, over the 170-word cap. Trim elsewhere if you use it.)

issues.problem: The URL returns a 403 (paywall), which the source-hygiene rule flags. It is still the canonical primary report, and its existence and content are confirmed through other coverage.
issues.fix: Keep the Bloomberg entry. The publisher field already says "(paywalled)", so no change is needed. Don't swap in a secondary repost.

Added two bespoke, restrained accents for story beats the stock kit doesn't quite cover: a soft low pulse under the counterfeit reveal and a subtle paper-rustle under the Bloomberg citation, both set low enough to stay felt, not heard.
